extension.summary: Friendly TV live channels, guide and on-demand for Kodi
extension.description:
Watch the live channel lineup, the programme guide and the on-demand catalogue from your own Friendly TV subscription, playing back through InputStream Adaptive with Widevine DRM.
Friendly TV runs on Revlet, and this addon speaks the same private endpoints as the web player at watch.frndlytv.com. Sign in with the email address and password you already use.
Features: * Live TV: every channel in your lineup, each showing what is on right now * Guide: a day of schedule per channel * Search across the channel lineup and the next twelve hours of guide * Record an episode or a whole series, and stop or delete a recording * The service's own Home, Movies, TV and My Stuff pages * Widevine playback through InputStream Adaptive, with no licence proxy -- Friendly TV's licence server speaks raw Widevine, so Kodi talks to it directly * Concurrent-stream slots are released when playback stops, so the account does not lock itself out * Optional IPTV Manager integration, putting the lineup and guide in Kodi's own TV section
Your subscription, your account, your lineup. Nothing is proxied through a third party.
extension.disclaimer: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Friendly Technologies or Frndly TV. This addon uses private, undocumented endpoints; use it with your own subscription.
extension.news: 2026.9.1 - First release - Playback on Kodi 21 is fixed. The DRM configuration was being written in the form only InputStream Adaptive 22.1.5 and newer reads, and ISA 21 does not warn about that -- it ignores the property and then refuses the stream with "InitializePeriod: Unhandled encrypted stream". The form is now chosen by the installed ISA version, and the log says which one went out. - Home shows its real rows. Friendly TV assembles that one screen from two endpoints, and the obvious one carries only the Live Now row, so Home was a single row of live channels. The rest come from the carousel endpoint, paged behind a cursor. - Search is Friendly TV's own catalogue search, paged, now that a capture reached the endpoint. Results mix pages to open with episodes that play, and each is routed by what it is. Shows, Movies and Channels filters sit at the top of the first page. - A film's page is no longer empty. Films and series are not built from the section shape the rest of the service uses: what plays them is a button in the page's content pane, and a film has nothing else on it at all. - A search that matches nothing says so instead of reporting an error. The search API answers no-matches with status false and a 404, which is a refusal in the protocol's terms and an empty list in anyone else's. - Search shows every result at once rather than a chain of "Next page" folders. It walks the pages itself, which for the totals this service returns is three to five requests. - A film plays in one click. Its card points at a page, but that page holds a single play button and nothing else, so the page is fetched and the button followed rather than listed as a folder to open. A series stays a folder, because it really does have seasons under it. - Shows, films and episodes are labelled as such for Kodi, so skins lay them out as shows and films instead of anonymous folders, and an episode carries its own name and its season and episode numbers. - Descriptions, cast, director, year and certificate now reach Kodi's own Information dialog. Friendly TV sends none of that with a listing -- it is empty on all but a handful of the 8191 cards captured, and lives only on each title's page -- so those pages are fetched for a listing's films and shows on a small pool of threads. One request per title is a real cost, so it is a setting with a cap, under Listings. - Picking the programme on the air in the guide asks whether to play live or start it over. Those turn out to be two different paths to the same endpoint rather than two kinds of request: the channel's gives the live edge, the programme's own is answered with the programme from its start. - Add to and remove from Favourites, on anything with a path -- films, shows, channels and guide airings alike. Only the verb that applies is offered, because the cards carry whether they are already in. These are Friendly TV's My Stuff, so they appear there and in its own apps. - A cast written as prose is read as names. Most pages send a plain list, but some send "Starring Marlon Brand, Karl Malden and Katy Jurado", which split on commas alone gave a cast whose first member was "Starring Marlon Brand" and whose last was "and Katy Jurado". - A title's page says whether it is already a favourite, so the right verb is shown there rather than both. - Recording reaches beyond the guide. 1803 of the captured cards say they may be recorded -- films and channels among them -- and each names the form to use, which is not the one a guide airing names. The card's own form code is what gets asked for. - A title opened from Information can be favourited from there too; its play button had no menu at all. Its page does not say whether it is already a favourite, so both verbs are offered rather than guessing one. - "More like this" on any film or show's context menu, and "Go to show" on a guide airing that belongs to a series -- the airing's overlay is the only thing that names the show it came from. - The guide carries descriptions, cast, artwork, episode numbers and certificates. The schedule endpoint sends a title and two times per airing and nothing else; everything readable is in each airing's overlay, fetched the same way and under the same setting as a listing's. - Continue Watching resumes. The service sends how far in you got as a fraction of the running time, and it was being read and thrown away, so that row restarted everything from the beginning. - A guide row for something not yet airing no longer fills the log with "InputStream: Error opening,". Those rows had an empty url, which Kodi treats as something to open rather than as inert; selecting one now says what it is and when it is on. - A lapsed session signs in once, not once per thread. Listings are fetched on a pool, so an expiry mid-listing would have had a dozen threads sign in at the same time, each invalidating the one before. - A film and a series describe themselves differently and both are now read correctly: a series has a description element and its subtitles are the episode on the air, while a film has no description element at all and its synopsis is the subtitle. Reading one rule for both left films blank and gave series their current episode's synopsis instead of their own. - Record an episode or a series, and stop or delete a recording, from the context menu on any guide airing. The service describes the choices and the addon echoes the chosen one back untouched, so it never has to know what the instruction strings mean. - The icon and fanart are Friendly TV's own logo, taken from the capture. - Live TV, the guide, and the service's own Home/Movies/TV/My Stuff pages. - Playback is Widevine DASH through InputStream Adaptive. Friendly TV's licence server takes a raw Widevine challenge and answers with raw licence bytes, which is exactly what ISA speaks, so there is no licence proxy in this addon and nothing listening on localhost. - Stream slots are handed back when playback stops. Friendly TV counts concurrent streams and only frees one when its poll key is posted back, so a client that never does locks the account out of its own subscription. - Optional IPTV Manager integration for Kodi's TV section.
